extracted.intended_audience: students, researchers, and librarians seeking museums, archives, and collection resources for comics and graphic novels
extracted.subtask_description: A university library research guide listing museums, archival collections, digital archives, and resources relevant to comics, graphic novels, political cartoons, and related materials, with scope and access notes for each resource.

rubrics_metrics.name: Webcomics Web Archive selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: This collection focuses on comics created specifically for the web and supplements the Library of Congress’ extensive holdings in both comic books, graphic novels, and original comic art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Webcomics selected for this collection include award-winning comics (Eisner Awards, Harvey Awards, Eagle Awards, and Shuster Awards) as well as webcomics that have significance in the field due to longevity, reputation, and subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Comic Museum scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides free access to hundreds of pre-1959 public domain comic books, uploaded by users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Site often includes historical research and commentary alongside high-quality scans; selection limited to material now in the public domain (pre-1959).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comic Book + Archive subject focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital archive of thousands of Golden and Silver Age comic books in the Superhero, Sci‑Fi, and Horror genres as well as fanzines and non-English publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes Golden and Silver Age material and genre-specific groupings (superhero, sci‑fi, horror), plus fanzines and materials in languages other than English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pulp Magazines Project purpose and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Open-access archive and digital research initiative for study and preservation of twentieth-century pulp magazines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides information and resources on publishing history, multiple search and discovery platforms, and an expanding library of high-quality, cover-to-cover digital facsimiles; aims to support research and preservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of 'underground comics (comix)'
rubrics_metrics.description: Underground comics are defined as comic books with adult themes discussing controversial topics and often mocking conventional society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical topics include feminism, marijuana legalization, Black Power, anti‑abortion and anti‑war themes, and gay and lesbian issues; the movement grew with 1960s–70s political and cultural ferment and often features work by influential author/illustrators (e.g., R. Crumb). Collections may include correspondence between staff and artists/dealers and are cataloged in library catalogs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library of Congress Comic Book Collection scope and access rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Collection includes U.S. and foreign comic books—over 5,000 titles totaling more than 100,000 issues; primarily original print books, most comprehensive from 1950 with scattered earlier issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comic books are circulated for use in the Newspaper and Current Periodical Room for those doing research; self‑service photocopying of comic books is prohibited. In some cases photocopies may be obtained through the Photoduplication Service of the Library of Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: University collection scope statements (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual university collections describe their specific emphases — time periods, types of materials, and special strengths (e.g., Bowling Green: commercially produced and independent/underground comics from 1930s–present; Brown: comics from early 1970s–1995 including translations and European comic art).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These scope statements function as selection/collection criteria: what titles/timeframes/formats are collected, notable strengths (small/independent publishers, translations, particular creators), and counts (e.g., estimated total items).

rubrics_metrics.name: Belgian Center for Comic Strip Art access and holdings
rubrics_metrics.description: Study library housing a very large collection of comic strips, allowing visitors access to albums, magazines, and reference works conserved at the center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reading room contains a selection of over 3,000 albums; albums are translated into over 36 languages; the collection can be viewed in the online catalog — emphasis on providing researcher access to large multilingual holdings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Michigan State University Comic Art Collection priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Holds over 200,000 items with important categories based on completeness and emphasis: U.S. comic books, international comics collection, newspaper strip books, and historical and critical materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Site includes lists of genres and titles within unique subgenres (advertising comic books, funny military comic books, prehistoric adventure comic books, etc.), signaling collection development and classification priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Billy Ireland Cartoon Library & Museum holdings and user resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Collection includes editorial cartoons, comic strips, comic books, graphic novels, sports cartoons, and magazine cartoons with extensive holdings (originals, books, serials, manuscript materials, clippings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finding aids (Cartoon Subject and Topic Files, Photograph Database) and digital resources (Cartoon Image Database) are provided; images of some collections are available online and educational resources/digital albums support teaching and research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Syracuse University Special Collections emphasis and organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Home to manuscript collections primarily of original artwork for daily comic strips and editorial cartoons, with strengths by era (strong in 1950s–1960s) and organization by creator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each entry contains biographical history, scope and content of subset, related material, and subject headings — indicating archival description best practices for usability.

rubrics_metrics.name: British Cartoon Archive research features and distribution policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides descriptions adding insight into cartoons and a search function enabling users to find cartoons by day, topic, or perception of personalities and events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can supply high‑resolution images for personal or educational use for a fee depending on copyright status; educators can create groups of cartoons for teaching and publish them on the web for students — practical access and reuse criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical search guidance for locating editorial cartoons in databases
rubrics_metrics.description: In ProQuest Advanced search under document type students can limit to 'editorial cartoon', then enter search terms; in ProQuest News and Newspapers Advanced search select 'editorial cartoon'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use document type filters and targeted search fields in major databases to find editorial cartoons effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Association and syndicate resources for editorial cartoons
rubrics_metrics.description: Association of American Editorial Cartoonists site allows searching for keywords and artists by year; New York Times Photos & Graphics includes editorial art from the New York Times Syndicate Cartoon Arts International.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional associations and syndicates provide searchable indexes and archives useful for identifying cartoonists, dates, and published editorial art.
